subject: Consent tiering & output title — order form redlines
messages:
From: Sophie Clark <sophie@novum.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Novum Legal <legal@novum.ai>; Procurement Team <procure@novum.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — output ownership / training opt-out

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal/procurement partners are reviewing the draft order form and asked for clarification on three items before we can sign:

1) Output ownership: The current order form language is unclear whether Novum would get any proprietary title to generated outputs used in our product. We need to understand whether Redwood assigns any ownership or whether use is limited to a license.

2) Training/data use: We are sensitive about our production prompts + user data being used to further train models. We want an explicit opt-out path and an indication of the operational controls to exclude our data from training.

3) Feedback license: We noticed a broad feedback clause — we need it scoped so internal product telemetry/redacted prompts can be used for service improvement only, not for marketing or model resale.

Can you share proposed redlines or the process/timeline for legal review? Procurement would like to close within Q3.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Clark
Head of AI Integrations | Novum AI
Attachments: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Clark <sophie@novum.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — output ownership / training opt-out

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. I pulled legal and product in to collate a proposed path so we can get procurement the options quickly.

Summary of our proposal (sending redlines):
- Output: default is a non-exclusive, worldwide license to use outputs for productization. For customers that purchase the "Exclusive Productization" add-on (one-time fee + higher commitment), we can provide exclusive output assignment limited to the output artifacts generated by the customer's inputs.
- Training/Data: provide a per-account data opt-out (no training) toggle. That will exclude customer prompts, inputs, and derived telemetry from our model training pipelines. Opt-out will be reflected in Order Form Exhibit A and requires a 30-day processing window.
- Feedback license: narrow the clause to allow Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified feedback and telemetry for service improvement and benchmarking only; no marketing attribution or resale of customer content.

I've attached a redlined order form for your legal team to review: novum_orderform_v2_redlines.docx.

Laura / Ben — could you review the attached and confirm the language for the opt-out timing and the exclusivity boundaries? I want to give Sophie a single consolidated answer for procurement.

Next step: Sophie, if this looks reasonable we'll prepare a DocuSign packet with the add-on term and marked Exhibit A.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: novum_orderform_v2_redlines.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: legal suggested language for Novum order form

Karthik / Ben — reviewed Sophie's ask and the redlines. High-level guidance and proposed wording below (I've attached a marked-up doc): legal_markups_orderform.docx.

1) Output ownership (proposed):
- "Ownership of Customer Inputs and Outputs: Customer retains ownership of Customer Inputs. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use Outputs for Customer's internal and commercial purposes. Exclusive assignment of Outputs is available only if Customer purchases the Exclusive Productization Add-on described in Exhibit B; such assignment is limited to Outputs generated while the add-on is in effect and does not include Redwood's pre-existing models or tooling."

Rationale: we should avoid blanket assignment of model IP but can carve a commercial path that customers pay for. Clear, bounded assignment reduces risk.

2) Training / data opt-out (proposed):
- "Training Opt-Out: Customer may elect to exclude its Customer Inputs and associated metadata from Redwood's model training pipelines by (a) selecting the 'Training Opt-Out' checkbox in the Order Form Exhibit A and (b) providing written notice to privacy@redwood.com. Redwood will implement the opt-out within thirty (30) days. Excluded data may still be processed for service provisioning, debugging, and security purposes but will not be used to train models or to improve model weights."

Rationale: 30-day window is operationally reasonable and we preserve minimal operational processing.

3) Feedback license (proposed):
- "Feedback and Telemetry: Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free right to use aggregated and de-identified Feedback and Telemetry for operating, improving, and benchmarking Redwood's services. Redwood will not use Customer Identifiable Content for marketing or third-party resale. 'Feedback' excludes raw Customer Inputs unless de-identified and aggregated such that re-identification is not reasonably practicable."

Operational notes: we should add a short consent-tiering table in Exhibit A showing pricing impact for the opt-out and the Exclusive Productization add-on. Procurement will require a one-line price delta. I recommend we draft Order Form Exhibit B with the add-on fee tiers.

Ben — can you draft the Exhibit B pricing options (SKU + delta) and the one-line procurement-friendly summary? I can then sign off on the legal text and we can route to Sophie.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: legal_markups_orderform.docx

Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — output ownership / training opt-out

Hi Sophie — looping back with the consolidated path after legal review. Thanks for your patience. Below is the customer-facing summary we propose; if Novum agrees we'll send a DocuSign packet with Exhibit A (opt-out checkbox) and Exhibit B (pricing table for Exclusive Productization).

Summary (final):
- Outputs: Redwood will grant Novum a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use Outputs for internal and commercial purposes. If Novum wants exclusive assignment of Outputs while the add-on is active, we offer a one-time Exclusive Productization add-on (details in Exhibit B). Assignment is limited to Outputs generated from Novum's Inputs while the add-on is in effect and does not transfer Redwood's underlying models or tooling.

- Training/Data: Novum may elect the Training Opt-Out by selecting the checkbox in Exhibit A and sending written notice to privacy@redwood.com. Redwood will operationally exclude Novum Customer Inputs and related telemetry from model training within thirty (30) days of receipt. Excluded data will still be processed for service provisioning, debugging, and security as necessary.

- Feedback License: Redwood will only use aggregated and de-identified Feedback/Telemetry data for service improvements and benchmarking. Redwood will not use Customer Identifiable Content for marketing purposes or third-party resale. Raw Customer Inputs will not be used for model training unless de-identified and aggregated per the Training Opt-Out rules.

Attachments: orderform_summary_table.pdf (one-page procurement summary) and the redlined order form have been uploaded for your review.

Next steps: if this is acceptable to Novum, reply with confirmation and any last open points. We will then prepare the DocuSign packet and a single-line pricing delta for procurement. Aim to get signatures in the next two weeks to hit your Q3 window.

Thanks and happy to jump on a quick call if it helps,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: orderform_summary_table.pdf; novum_orderform_v2_redlines.docx
